beats: In 1876, it rained meat in Kentucky!
Mrs. Crouch was outside making soap when chunks of raw flesh started falling from a clear blue sky.
For a few minutes, it covered a strip of land the size of a football field.
The biggest pieces were four inches across.
And they did the obvious thing. They tasted it!
Their verdict: mutton. Or maybe venison.
One scientist insisted it was a kind of algae.
Then the microscopes came out. It was lung, muscle and cartilage.
One doctor said the lung came from either a horse, or a human baby.
Vultures throw up their meals to lighten the load, so they can take off faster.
A flock passing overhead had simply lost its lunch.
Which means two men in Kentucky had tasted vulture vomit!
And a piece of it is still kept in a jar.
